projects.title: Solvix
projects.what: An AI-powered DSA practice tracker that automatically imports your Codeforces and LeetCode history, scores which topics have decayed, and generates a daily study plan with spaced-repetition reminders. No manual logging required.
projects.hardPart: Free-tier hosting sleeps when idle, so daily plans and reminders run on an external GitHub Actions cron instead of an in-process timer.
notes: The backend sleeps when idle, so reminders and plan generation run on an external cron rather than an in-process timer.
Topic scoring treats Codeforces and LeetCode differently, since only one of them records failed attempts.
Repeated wrong submissions collapse into a single attempt, so retry-spam doesn't distort the score.

projects.title: Real-Time Drowsiness Detection
projects.what: A computer vision system that monitors a live webcam feed, tracks facial landmarks, and computes Eye Aspect Ratio in real time to detect fatigue, triggering an audio alert when eyes stay closed past a threshold.
projects.hardPart: Tuning the EAR threshold and frame count to catch real drowsiness without firing on ordinary blinks, while staying fast enough for live video.

projects.title: Secure Auth System
projects.what: A Spring Boot authentication system implementing user registration, login, and role-based access control (USER/ADMIN), with BCrypt password encryption and session-managed protected routes.
projects.hardPart: Designing role-based access, BCrypt storage, and session handling into the Spring Security layer from the start, rather than bolting security on afterwards.

projects.title: Emergency Ambulance Route Optimizer
projects.what: A dispatch system that answers two questions from a patient's location: which hospital they should go to, and the fastest road route there. It then sends the nearest available ambulance and tracks it live on an OpenStreetMap network.
projects.hardPart: Edge weights are travel time rather than distance, so a congested shortcut loses to a clear detour — on the demo network a 3.9km direct route is rejected for an 8.4km one that is genuinely faster.
notes: Dijkstra, A*, the min-heap ranking and the triage queue are written from scratch — no networkx, no shortest-path library.
A* is measurably cheaper on the same route: 286 node expansions against Dijkstra's 379 on the 433-junction network, which /route?algo=compare reports directly.

Hospital ranking balances distance against capacity — a hospital with no spare beds is ranked as if it were three minutes further, enough to break ties but never enough to send a patient past a much closer one.
Triage cannot starve anyone: severity sets your place in the queue, and every ten minutes of waiting improves it by a full level.
An ambulance's position is derived from elapsed time along its computed route, so it needs no background job and survives a restart.
